chapter: Style and old New Orleans customs
title: Quadrilles and who still has the music
summary: Quadrilles were going out by the time he began; he never played them, and Peter Bocage might have sets.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: What about quadrilles? Were they playing any quadrilles when you started?

Not when I started. Well, yeah, they were playing, but I mean I wasn't. They were still dancing, quadrilles, shatters, and walls. But I never played quadrilles. During my time, coming along, the quadrilles was going out. And now and then somebody will hire a band and ask them, can they play a quadrilles? Well, if they never played it, they can't play it. And Peter Bocards is the honest man around here that I know now that might have a couple of sets of quadrilles that he could rent to a band, you know, or play with a band or something like that. But you know, now Percy, Percy might have some because his daddy had all types of really couldn't be in a teacher. He might have some, but I can tell you, I teach younger musicians about a quadrilles that look at you like you ain't got good things. You don't see no more shadows and you don't see no more walls. People don't dance together now. The boys be jumping on one side, the floor and the girls be jumping on the other side. I don't know when they ever get together to call it a dance. Beats me.
